conversations.title: Parkinson's drastically changed how they have sex. They're not alone. - USA Today
conversations.reply: Parkinson's changing someone's sex life shouldn't be news; the real story is how few partners stay long enough for that conversation. Testimony from disabled daters says the same pattern: all the right words, then silence once things get complicated. That gap is why Able2Love exists.

conversations.title: Forget Tinder: LinkedIn is the new place to find love - Ynetnews
conversations.reply: Trustworthy is a low bar when the competition is mainstream dating apps that let people vanish the moment a visible disability enters the chat. A polished profile photo doesn't fix that. Only actual honesty does, which is the whole design brief behind this app.

conversations.title: The founder of Hinge raised $18M to build a new AI dating service, Overtone - TechCrunch
conversations.reply: Another dating app, another eighteen million, still not a line about the daters mainstream platforms have spent years quietly filtering out. Years of testimony from disabled daters say the industry keeps innovating around the same gap instead of closing it.

conversations.title: Leeds Pride 2026 Set to Draw 60,000 as City Marks 20 Years of Celebration - Public Sector Executive
conversations.reply: Sixty thousand people through a city centre is a good headline. The real test is whether every venue and stage on that route has a step-free way in, because a Pride that leaves wheelchair users outside asking someone to check isn't pride for everyone.

conversations.title: Column | Asking Eric: Neighbors react badly to person with autism disorder - The Washington Post
conversations.reply: Neighbours reacting badly to autism is not a personality clash, it's ableism with a different postcode. It surfaces at work, on doorsteps and, endlessly, in the testimony of disabled daters trying to get a straight answer out of someone.

target_reply: Molly Burke's reach says more about mainstream platforms' failures than luck: blind creators still get treated as niche by apps built entirely around a swipe and a photo grid. Able2Love exists for exactly the daters those platforms overlook, and that argument belongs in front of an audience that already trusts her.
funding: Nothing new today. Standing routes worth chasing: UnLtd (unltd.org.uk), Access to Work (gov.uk), and the Stelios Awards (opening around March).
moment: July is Disability Pride Month. Mark it properly by testing whether the venue hosting your own Pride afterparty could actually let a wheelchair user through the front door, not round the back past the bins.
